intended_object: The standard comparison morphism ΩΣX → X in a Frobenius exact category, taken from the docstring and the surrounding section. Take the suspension conflation X ↣ I(X) ↠ ΣX and the loop conflation ΩΣX ↣ P(ΣX) ↠ ΣX. Lift the deflation P(ΣX) ↠ ΣX through I(X) ↠ ΣX, which is possible because P(ΣX) is projective. The lift induces a map on kernels, and this map is a representative of the inverse of the unit X ≅ ΩΣX in the stable category.
explanation:
The body follows the textbook construction exactly. `loopSuspensionInvMiddleMap` is a lift P(ΣX) → I(X) of the loop deflation along the suspension deflation. It is obtained from `factorThru`, using that the loop object P(ΣX) is projective. Composing the loop inflation ΩΣX ↣ P(ΣX) with this lift gives a map whose composite with the suspension deflation is zero, since inflation followed by deflation is zero. The map therefore factors uniquely through the kernel X of the suspension conflation. This is the usual "induced map on kernels".

The map in C depends on the chosen lift, but it is well defined up to maps that factor through projectives. The theorems right after it show that its image in the stable category is a two-sided inverse of `toLoopSuspension`, which matches the docstring.

The construction needs exactly the stated setting: an exact category with enough projectives that is Frobenius, which supplies Σ and Ω. It is no narrower than that. Mathlib has no counterpart, since it does not define exact or Frobenius categories or their stable categories.
